question: Which native drag owner and UI policies should block dragging and drop indicators reuse?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, frozen from status at fe0e9599a6 on 2026-10-04 (39 units), and judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was open as pursue-not-adopted at queue position 36. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: Block drag is native. A handle calls editor.api.dom.drag.start, the Editable resolves each drop and runs editor.api.transfer, and the kit paints useDropIndicator, with no provider, manager or backend.
Copied handles follow the schema. Every selectable block-content element gets one at any depth, only the innermost hovered one shows, and copied UI never lists plugin types or depths.
One per-edge landing law serves hover, drop, keyboard move and file drop, so the indicator never shows an edge the drop refuses.
Moves are lossless or refused; copy intent, read-only sources, two views and roots keep their transfer laws.
dragover cost stays flat with document size.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-10-02 landing review, its execution and the 2026-10-03 panel repair execution (21 browser cases in three engines over five warm runs, resolveDropTarget flat at 0.03 to 0.05 ms from 300 to 15,000 blocks, a handle-render budget), and the 2026-10-02 library review. Rechecked on the live tree that landing.ts, transfer.ts, dom-drag.ts and dnd.tsx are committed (4e16eada7d and 209bbb7ff3), that feature plugins contribute transferVeto and List contributes an around redirect, that UNDRAGGABLE_PLUGINS, getDraggableContainer and the copied payloadOf are gone, and that touch drag is an app-owned pointer driver by decision.
summary: The job is native block drag with one Plite transfer law for hover, drop, keyboard steps and file drops, feature limits the schema cannot state, and copied handles that follow the schema. Live committed source does exactly that. landAt checks identity, a redirect-only landing read, canPlaceAt and every transferVeto. Column, Table, Details, Footnote and Upload contribute vetoes, List keeps one around(transfer.landing) redirect, and dnd.tsx has no plugin list, depth table or payload copy. The strongest replacement, a private Pragmatic Drag and Drop driver, stays a separate deferral with no recorded native-driver defect it would delete, and doctrine says block drag needs no provider, manager or backend. Other lanes (schema prefix grammar for details summaries, schema root-only footnote definitions, a table data attribute instead of dnd.tsx importing BaseTablePlugin) are small, already-owned follow-ups, not a better direction. The long Open findings list is edge-case bug and scale work with named owners, not an API or architecture question.

reconciliation.reason: Keep the native driver. The Pragmatic Drag and Drop (PDD) comparison stays optional evidence that reopens only the driver choice, and only on a measured native-driver maintenance cost.

alternatives: Keeping the adopted design wins. The root-only default, Column and Table widening middleware and the copied depth policy are gone, and blockquote, details and footnote content take drops.

Replacing the native driver with a private Pragmatic Drag and Drop (PDD) lifecycle is not justified now. Source anchors, MIME capture, view routing, admission and scheduling stay editor work, and no recorded driver defect in the open list is a browser quirk PDD would own. It remains the 2026-10-02 library deferral, not a reason to reopen landing.

The plan's Defaults reject pushing details-summary-first and root-only footnote definitions into schema grammar for now, because stored documents would need migration. The plan tracks both as owned open findings.
This review rejects moving handle policy or a drag engine back into a package or Plite core, because doctrine keeps copied DndKit as optional product UI over neutral Plite APIs.

A cross-feature cleanup would replace dnd.tsx's BaseTablePlugin selector with a table-owned DOM attribute that CSS reads and delete the dnd-to-table import. It is a small copied-UI follow-up, not material to the scope question.
proofLimits: This was a source review only, and nothing was run. Landing and handle files are committed (git status clean). BaseTablePlugin.ts and grid.ts hold another session's staged edits that do not touch the vetoes. Browser receipts are Playwright-emulated drags on a development build, with no native OS drag, Safari, touch device or production build. The PDD retention rests on the 2026-10-02 library review's source comparison, not a run.
